description.value: This study examined methamphetamine-induced changes in corticostriatal gray matter and their relationships with inhibitory control and dopaminergic markers in vervet monkeys.
Fourteen adult male vervet monkeys were assigned to methamphetamine or saline exposure and assessed before and after an escalating 31-day dosing regimen.

spans.text: Methamphetamine hydrochloride was purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (St Louis MO).

Structural magnetic resonance images and positron emission tomography (PET) scans, assessing dopamine D2-like receptor and transporter availability, were acquired in monkeys trained to acquire, retain and reverse three-choice visual discrimination problems before and after exposure to an escalating dose regimen of methamphetamine (or saline, as a control).

description.value: Monkeys were trained to acquire, retain and reverse visual discrimination problems using three visual stimuli, with performance measured by trials required to reach criterion in the reversal phase.

spans.text: visual stimuli

value: Number of trials required to reach criterion in the reversal phase

spans.text: The number of trials required to reach criterion in the reversal phase was the primary dependent measure.

instructions.value: Subjects learned stimulus-reward contingencies through feedback, completed acquisition and retention phases, and then completed a reversal phase in which the previously rewarded stimulus was no longer rewarded.
